result.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories
result.comment: This paper is accepted to NeurIPS 2026 PhysWorldAI Workshop
result.summary: Everyday smartphone walks offer a scalable source of indoor geometry, but their motion traces drift and their radio measurements are distorted by multipath. We present Walks2Maps, a physics-guided framework that reconstructs a shared metric map from Wi-Fi round-trip-time (RTT) and motion observations, without a floor plan, surveyed access-point (AP) coordinates, or position labels. Walks2Maps jointly estimates pedestrian trajectories, AP locations, and per-trajectory stride scales, then recovers the pathway layout from the reconstructed paths. Shared AP observations connect walks recorded in different local frames, while metric ranges constrain their relative geometry and scale. An asymmetric range loss accommodates multipath-induced excess delay. On 22 phone trajectories collected along 11 routes on an office floor with 30 APs, Walks2Maps achieves median AP and trajectory errors of 0.87 m and 0.89 m, respectively, and a walked-area F1 score of 0.985. Ablations show that radio similarity can recognize places while still producing a distorted map; retaining the metric information in RTT resolves this ambiguity. Asymmetric modeling further reduces AP error by 54% relative to a symmetric loss. These results demonstrate how radio and motion measurements can jointly reveal indoor geometry without a dedicated mapping survey. We will release the dataset and toolkit.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Walks2Maps，从众包 Wi-Fi RTT 与运动轨迹重建室内共享度量地图，无需平面图、AP 坐标或位置标签，联合估计行人轨迹、AP 位置与步幅尺度，并用非对称距离损失应对多径时延。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“仅靠相似性可识别场所但得到扭曲地图、需保留度量信息消歧”的发现，可能与 LVR 中内部状态是否保留几何与任务必要信息、以及视觉证据筛选的可辨识性问题类比，但领域较远，仅供核查。
